title: The 10 Best-Selling Trucks of 2026 (And What the Ranking Hides)

scenes.text: The ten best-selling pickup trucks in America sold more than two million, one hundred eighty-seven thousand units in nine months. One of them is up forty percent. One is down thirteen percent in its heavy-duty version. And number two is closing in on number one faster than anyone expected. This is the real ranking of the best-selling trucks of twenty twenty-six, and what the ranking hides.
scenes.caption: TOP 10 TRUCKS OF 2026

scenes.text: Every year, the same question gets asked. Which truck is really number one? And every year, the answer is the same, with one small change. But this year, the change is bigger than usual. We took the nine-month sales table that Pickup Truck Talk published for twenty twenty-six, covering January through September, and ranked the ten best-selling trucks. Then we looked for the twist in each one.
scenes.caption: JAN-SEP 2026 SALES TABLE

scenes.text: Before the countdown, one number sets the scale. The ten trucks on this list add up to two million, one hundred eighty-seven thousand, seven hundred fifty. The top three alone, the Ford F-Series, the Chevrolet Silverado and the Ram, are fifty-nine percent of that. So the market is concentrated at the top. But the ranking is not frozen, and the changes happen in the middle. Every number comes from a published source, listed in the description.
scenes.caption: TOP 3 = 59% OF THE TOP 10

scenes.text: A note on method. We count each model line as one truck, including its light-duty and heavy-duty versions. The Ford F-Series is shown without the electric Lightning, as the table does, and where Ford's own number differs, we say so. We rank by sales through September, not by the last quarter. And we leave out the electric trucks and the medium-duty trucks, which sell in much smaller numbers and have their own videos. Let's start at the bottom.
scenes.caption: METHOD: JAN-SEP 2026, U.S. SALES

scenes.text: Number ten is the Ford Ranger. Through nine months of twenty twenty-six, Ford sold fifty-one thousand, six hundred thirty Rangers, up six point nine percent from forty-eight thousand, two hundred seventy-eight a year earlier. It is the smallest number on the list. But look at the quarters. Sales fell nearly ten percent in the second quarter, to sixteen thousand, two hundred ninety-four, and then jumped almost fifteen percent in the third, to seventeen thousand, five hundred sixty-one.
scenes.caption: 10. RANGER: 51,630

scenes.text: That is the twist. The truck at the bottom of the ranking is a truck with a roller coaster year. It is up for nine months, down in one quarter, and up in the next. If you only read one quarter, you would draw the wrong conclusion twice. The Ranger tells you why a nine-month table is more honest than a headline about one quarter, and why a small number is not the same as a weak truck.
scenes.caption: Q2 -9.8%. Q3 +14.8%.

scenes.text: Number nine is the Nissan Frontier, and it is the fastest-growing truck on the list. Nissan sold sixty-six thousand, five hundred thirteen Frontiers through nine months, up thirty-nine point six percent from forty-seven thousand, six hundred thirty. In the third quarter, it sold twenty-three thousand, four hundred twelve, up thirty-seven and a half percent. No other truck in this ranking comes close to that rate of growth.
scenes.caption: 9. FRONTIER: 66,513 (+39.6%)

scenes.text: The twist is who this truck belongs to. Nissan is the same company that ended its full-size Titan after the twenty twenty-four model year, and the Titan sold just thirteen trucks in the same nine months. The company lost a full-size truck and gained a midsize one. The Fast Lane Truck credited the Frontier's naturally aspirated V six engine, and said buyers seem to be listening. A simple engine, in a simple truck, is selling.
scenes.caption: TITAN: 13 TRUCKS. FRONTIER: UP 40%.

scenes.text: Number eight is the Chevrolet Colorado. Through nine months, Chevrolet sold seventy-two thousand, eight hundred sixty-three, down five point eight percent from seventy-seven thousand, three hundred ninety. It is the only midsize truck from a Detroit company in the top ten besides the Ranger, and it is the second best seller in its segment, behind the Tacoma by a wide margin.
scenes.caption: 8. COLORADO: 72,863 (-5.8%)

scenes.text: Here is the twist. In the third quarter, the Colorado sold twenty-five thousand, one hundred seventy, up two point four percent. So the truck that lost ground for the year was growing again in the latest quarter. And its twin, the GMC Canyon, rose twenty percent for the nine months, to thirty-three thousand, five hundred forty-five. Same truck, same factory, opposite directions. The Colorado is a reminder that two badges can tell two different stories.
scenes.caption: Q3: COLORADO +2.4%

scenes.text: Number seven is the Toyota Tundra. Toyota sold one hundred ten thousand and eighty Tundras through nine months, down eight tenths of a percent from one hundred ten thousand, nine hundred forty-five. It is the only full-size truck from a Japanese company still being built, and it is the smallest of the five full-size trucks in this ranking. But the number is very stable, quarter after quarter.
scenes.caption: 7. TUNDRA: 110,080 (-0.8%)

scenes.text: The twist is who beats it. The Tundra is Toyota's full-size flagship, and it sold fewer trucks than the Toyota Tacoma, the midsize one, by a margin of almost two to one. And the Ford Maverick, a compact truck, outsold it too, with one hundred twenty-three thousand, six hundred eighty-one. A full-size truck can be a very good truck and still not be the best-seller of its own family.
scenes.caption: TUNDRA: BEATEN BY ITS OWN TACOMA

scenes.text: Number six is the Ford Maverick, the compact pickup that now outsells every midsize truck except the Tacoma. Ford sold one hundred twenty-three thousand, six hundred eighty-one Mavericks through nine months, up two point three percent. In the third quarter alone it sold forty-one thousand, nine hundred seventy, up twenty point four percent. And the Maverick Hybrid was seventy-four thousand, three hundred of those trucks, a record for the model.
scenes.caption: 6. MAVERICK: 123,681

scenes.text: The twist is the hybrid. About sixty percent of every Maverick sold through the third quarter was a hybrid, and in the third quarter alone, about two thirds. The smallest truck from Ford is selling the most advanced powertrain. And it outsold the entire Hyundai Santa Cruz many times over. The Santa Cruz sold fourteen thousand, eight hundred eleven in the same period. A small truck can win, when it is the right small truck.
scenes.caption: MAVERICK HYBRID: 74,300

scenes.text: Number five is the Toyota Tacoma, the best-selling midsize truck in America by a very large margin. Toyota sold two hundred fourteen thousand, eight hundred seventy-five Tacomas through nine months, up five point one percent from two hundred four thousand, four hundred sixty-four. The next midsize truck, the Chevrolet Colorado, sold seventy-two thousand, eight hundred sixty-three. The Tacoma sold almost three times as many.
scenes.caption: 5. TACOMA: 214,875 (+5.1%)

scenes.text: And here is the twist. The Tacoma is number five on this list, right behind four full-size trucks, and it is the only truck in the top five that is not full-size. The Tacoma grew nearly sixteen percent in the first half, to one hundred forty-three thousand, eight hundred forty-eight, and then slipped three and a half percent in the third quarter, to seventy-one thousand and twenty-seven.
scenes.caption: H1 +15.8%. Q3 -3.5%.

scenes.text: Number four is the GMC Sierra. Through nine months, GMC sold two hundred fifty-two thousand, six hundred thirty-nine Sierras, up three tenths of a percent from two hundred fifty-one thousand, eight hundred forty-five. Almost perfectly flat. In the third quarter, it sold eighty-four thousand, nine hundred twenty-nine, down six tenths of a percent. If you want a truck with a steady, predictable record, this is it.
scenes.caption: 4. SIERRA: 252,639 (+0.3%)

scenes.text: The twist is hidden inside the number. The light-duty Sierra rose four point four percent, to one hundred seventy-four thousand, three hundred ninety-three. The heavy-duty Sierra fell seven point seven percent, to seventy-eight thousand, two hundred forty-six. A flat total hides a split. The everyday truck is growing, and the work truck is shrinking. That is a pattern we will see again, in the next two trucks.
scenes.caption: LD +4.4%. HD -7.7%.

scenes.text: Number three is the Ram, and it is the biggest story of the year. Ram sold three hundred twenty-five thousand, three hundred forty-eight pickups through nine months, up twenty-four percent from two hundred sixty-two thousand, three hundred eighty-six. That is an extra sixty-two thousand, nine hundred sixty-two trucks. In the third quarter alone, Ram sold one hundred seventeen thousand, seven hundred fifty-seven, up thirty-three point seven percent.
scenes.caption: 3. RAM: 325,348 (+24%)

scenes.text: Look inside the number for the twist. The light-duty Ram sold two hundred two thousand, one hundred forty-seven, up forty-one percent. In the third quarter, the light-duty Ram jumped seventy-three percent, from forty-four thousand, three hundred forty-nine to seventy-six thousand, six hundred fifty. The heavy-duty Ram, meanwhile, rose only three point four percent. The growth is in the everyday truck. And it happened in a year in which Ram canceled its electric truck.
scenes.caption: RAM LD: +41%

scenes.text: Number two is the Chevrolet Silverado. Chevrolet sold four hundred thirteen thousand, three hundred eighty-three Silverados through nine months, down seven tenths of a percent from four hundred sixteen thousand, two hundred ninety. In the third quarter, it sold one hundred forty-four thousand, four hundred ninety-nine, up four point nine percent.
scenes.caption: 2. SILVERADO: 413,383 (-0.7%)

scenes.text: And now the twist. The light-duty Silverado grew six point five percent, to two hundred seventy-nine thousand, six hundred fourteen. The heavy-duty Silverado fell thirteen percent, from one hundred fifty-three thousand, seven hundred fifty to one hundred thirty-three thousand, seven hundred sixty-nine. The same split as the Sierra, only bigger. And the gap between the Silverado and the Ram, which was one hundred fifty-three thousand, nine hundred four trucks a year ago, is now eighty-eight thousand and thirty-five.
scenes.caption: GAP TO RAM: 153,904 TO 88,035

scenes.text: Number one, as always, is the Ford F-Series. Without the Lightning, Ford sold five hundred fifty-six thousand, seven hundred thirty-eight through nine months, down six point eight percent from five hundred ninety-seven thousand, five hundred forty-six. Ford's own release, which includes the Lightning, shows five hundred sixty-one thousand, five hundred eight. Either way, it is about a quarter of everything on this list, and ten times the Ranger.
scenes.caption: 1. F-SERIES: 556,738 (-6.8%)

scenes.text: Here is the twist. The F-Series lost forty thousand, eight hundred eight trucks in a year. That is a very large number. And it is still number one by one hundred forty-three thousand trucks over the Silverado. In the third quarter, it recovered, selling two hundred three thousand, four hundred eighteen, up two point nine percent, and in September, Ford sold sixty-seven thousand, four hundred forty-eight, up two point four percent. The king is wounded, but it is still the king.
scenes.caption: Q3: +2.9%. SEPT: 67,448.

scenes.text: Now let's look at the same list a year ago, because the ranking tells another story when you compare. In the first nine months of twenty twenty-five, the order of the top seven was exactly the same. Ford, Chevrolet, Ram, GMC, Toyota Tacoma, Ford Maverick and Toyota Tundra. The top of the table did not change places. The only changes happened in the numbers, and at the very bottom.
scenes.query: Ford F-150 Chevrolet Silverado Ram 1500 pickups
scenes.caption: TOP 7: SAME ORDER AS 2025

scenes.text: At the bottom, there is a swap. A year ago, the Ford Ranger sold forty-eight thousand, two hundred seventy-eight, and the Nissan Frontier sold forty-seven thousand, six hundred thirty. The Ranger was ahead. This year the Frontier sold sixty-six thousand, five hundred thirteen, and the Ranger fifty-one thousand, six hundred thirty. The Frontier overtook the Ranger, with a lead of almost fifteen thousand trucks. That is the only rank change in the entire list.
scenes.caption: FRONTIER PASSES RANGER

scenes.text: And there is a third change that the ranking cannot show, because the order stayed the same. The gap between the Ram and the GMC Sierra. A year ago, the Ram sold two hundred sixty-two thousand, three hundred eighty-six, and the Sierra two hundred fifty-one thousand, eight hundred forty-five, a gap of ten thousand, five hundred forty-one trucks. This year the gap is seventy-two thousand, seven hundred nine. Same positions, very different distance.
scenes.caption: RAM VS SIERRA: GAP 10,541 TO 72,709

scenes.text: That is the lesson of any ranking. A list tells you who is ahead, but not how fast they are moving, and not how far apart they are. Two trucks can hold the same position for years while one of them is quietly pulling away. When you read a ranking of the best-selling trucks, look for the gaps, because the gaps are where the news is.
scenes.caption: READ THE GAPS, NOT THE RANKS

scenes.text: So how should a buyer use a ranking like this? Not as a shopping list. Use it as a check. If a truck is in the top five, it means service, parts and resale demand are likely to be easy to find, because a lot of trucks are on the road. If a truck is falling in the ranking, ask why, and ask the dealer whether the model is going to be updated. And if a truck is rising fast, check whether the price is rising with it.
scenes.caption: HOW TO USE A RANKING

scenes.text: There is a simple way to do that. Take the truck you like, and look up three numbers. The sales for the first nine months of this year, the sales for the same months last year, and the change in the latest quarter. If all three point the same way, you have a clear signal. If they point in different directions, like the Ranger, you have a truck in motion, and you should ask more questions before you sign.
scenes.caption: THREE NUMBERS TO CHECK

scenes.text: So what does the ranking hide? Three things. First, it hides the split between light-duty and heavy-duty. Both Chevrolet and GMC grew the everyday truck and lost the work truck, and Ram did the opposite in volume, growing the everyday truck fast and the work truck slowly. Second, it hides the quarters. Nine months tell the direction, and the third quarter shows the turn. And third, it hides the small numbers.
scenes.query: Ford F-250 Chevrolet Silverado HD Ram 2500 pickups
scenes.caption: WHAT THE RANKING HIDES

scenes.text: Because just below this list are trucks that matter. The Honda Ridgeline sold thirty-seven thousand and twenty-eight, down one percent. The Jeep Gladiator sold thirty thousand, nine hundred forty-four, down nearly twenty percent. And the Hyundai Santa Cruz sold fourteen thousand, eight hundred eleven, down twenty-eight percent. These are not in the top ten, but their numbers show where the market is going cold.
scenes.caption: BELOW THE LIST: RIDGELINE, GLADIATOR

scenes.text: There is one more twist, and it is about the price. According to Kelley Blue Book, the average full-size pickup sold for sixty-seven thousand, four hundred forty-six dollars in August, up two point one percent. So the trucks on this ranking are selling in huge numbers, at prices that are higher than ever. The pickup is not a cheap product in twenty twenty-six. It is a very expensive product that Americans keep buying.
scenes.caption: AVERAGE FULL-SIZE PRICE: $67,446

scenes.text: Let's use two of the numbers we already saw to make the point about size. The Ford F-Series sold five hundred fifty-six thousand, seven hundred thirty-eight trucks in nine months, and the Ranger sold fifty-one thousand, six hundred thirty. That is why a loss can mean very different things. The F-Series lost forty thousand, eight hundred eight trucks and still led the table by a wide gap. A small truck losing a few thousand could be a real problem. A big truck losing a few thousand might be nothing. Always compare a change to the size of the truck.
scenes.caption: A LOSS MEANS DIFFERENT THINGS

scenes.text: Here is a mistake that a lot of shoppers make. They see a truck that is up twenty-four percent and assume it must be the best truck. But the Ram's growth is a sales number, not a quality number. It tells you that many people chose it, and the reasons could be price, timing, a new model or a good offer. A sales table cannot tell you about reliability or comfort. For those, you need owner reviews, recall records and a test drive, and the sales table is only the start.
scenes.caption: SALES ARE NOT QUALITY

scenes.text: Before you buy any of these trucks, check the recall record for the exact vehicle. It takes a few minutes. Find the vehicle identification number, which is on the plate at the base of the windshield and on the door sticker. Enter it on the government recall lookup, and it will tell you whether any safety recall is open on that exact truck. A popular truck is not a truck without recalls, and a dealer should be happy to show you that the check is clean.
scenes.caption: CHECK THE VIN FOR RECALLS

scenes.text: The door sticker answers another question that the sales table cannot. It lists the weight rating of the truck and the payload, which is how much weight the truck can carry. For towing, the sticker and the owner manual matter more than the brand name. A heavy-duty Sierra and a light-duty Sierra share a name, but they are different tools. So when you read that the heavy-duty trucks fell and the light-duty ones rose, remember that the buyer who needs the work truck must check the sticker on the exact truck.
scenes.caption: READ THE DOOR STICKER

scenes.text: Who does each part of this list suit? If you want the biggest network of parts and service, the top three, the Ford F-Series, the Chevrolet Silverado and the Ram, hold fifty-nine percent of the list, so there are a lot of them on the road. If you want a midsize truck, the Tacoma is far ahead, and the Frontier is the fast riser. If you want something small and efficient, the Maverick is the story, with the hybrid at about sixty percent of its sales.
scenes.caption: WHO THE LIST SUITS

scenes.text: And who should wait? If you are looking at a truck that is falling, like the Colorado for the nine months or the Ranger in one quarter, do not panic and do not rush. Wait for one more quarter of numbers, and ask the dealer whether anything is changing in the model. A falling number is a question, not a verdict. The same goes for a truck that is rising fast. Let the numbers settle, compare the same trim on the same day at two dealers, and then decide.
scenes.caption: WAIT FOR ONE MORE QUARTER

scenes.text: So what should you check before you buy a truck in twenty twenty-seven? First, look at the sales of the exact version, not the model. A heavy-duty truck and a light-duty truck from the same brand can move in opposite directions. Second, look at the latest quarter, not only the year. And third, remember that the best-selling truck is not automatically the best truck for you. Popularity helps resale and service. It does not choose your trailer.
scenes.caption: CHECK 1, 2 AND 3
scenes.chapter: What to check before you buy in 2027

scenes.text: We put all of this into a checklist, the Twenty Twenty-Seven Truck Buyer's Guide. It covers the numbers to check, the questions to ask a dealer, and the warning signs we walked through. The link is in the description and in the pinned comment. If you want to know which trucks are the most reliable, according to the data, subscribe, because that is coming soon. Thanks for watching.
